description: One leg, all the way down, all the way up. Your clean pistol count is the test, and these five mistakes are what quietly destroy your ankle and knee leverage: the lifted heel, the collapsing knee, and the bounce out of the bottom. Take the test, then fix the leaks.

scenes.narration: One leg. | Free leg forward, | floating, always floating. | Sink down slowly | to your full depth. | Pause at the bottom. | One honest second. | Stand back up | without bouncing, | without grabbing, | without the free foot | ever touching down. | That is one | clean pistol. | Count them | until the first mistake. | The heel lifts. | The knee caves. | The free foot | slaps the floor | to save you. | When form breaks, | stop counting. | That clean count | is your number. | Keep it safe. | Five mistakes | are taxing | your depth, | and we name them | at the end. | | Warm the ankles before this | clock starts, two minutes of | knee-to-wall work and deep squats. | A cold chain reads stiffer | and weaker than the real | one, and you are grading | your leverage, not your warm-up | discipline. | Also test on a flat, | grippy floor in the same | shoes or bare feet every | time. | The pistol is a measurement | instrument built from your body, | and instruments are calibrated or | they are ornaments.

scenes.label: CLEAN FULL PISTOLS IS THE LINE
scenes.narration: Here is the line. Three clean pistols in a row, full depth, heel down, bottom paused, on your weaker leg, is certified single-leg leverage. Zero clean is the world's most common score, and it usually means a mistake is spending your depth before you reach it. Five or more clean, either leg, puts you in pistol country permanently. The clean rule is ruthless here because pistol mistakes are photogenic: a heel-lifted, bouncing, knee-caving rep looks deep in a screenshot and scores zero in this test, and your ankle and knee know the difference even when your followers do not. Record the height of any assistance you used, in centimeters, next to the count. A clean pistol to a low box and a clean pistol to the floor are cousins, not twins, and the log that confuses them will lie to you in thirty days. Precision here is a kindness to your future self, who will otherwise stand in the same spot wondering whether he improved or merely forgot what last month's test actually was.
scenes.sub: 0 clean: a mistake spends your depth - 5+: pistol country

lines: The ankle bends so the knee can travel.
Every shortcut breaks the chain somewhere.
beats.title: TWO HINGES, ONE CHAIN

scenes.narration: The chain, one more time, because every mistake is a break in it. The ankle bends so the knee can travel forward and your weight stays over your foot. The knee then lifts your whole body from its deepest, worst-leveraged angle. Break the chain anywhere and the failure appears somewhere else: a stiff ankle tips you backward, a caving knee dumps the load sideways, a bouncing bottom skips the angle where strength is built. The pistol is not one exercise with five mistakes. It is one chain with five weak links, and the test finds whichever link you brought. Your arms, reaching forward, are part of this chain too, and their job is ballast. They shift mass ahead of your foot to counterbalance the hips traveling back, and a lazy arm position quietly steals depth by letting your weight fall behind your base. Reach hard, like you are offering someone a tray. It looks like a detail. At full depth, with everything at its limit, details are the whole difference between a hold and a sit-down.

beats.text: THE KNEE CAVE IS A LEAK

scenes.narration: Watch the knee cave get priced. Let the knee dive inward on the way up and the rep suddenly works, because the load slid off the thigh's strongest line onto passive structures that do not get tired, or stronger, only irritated. Score it honestly and three tracking-straight pistols become one caving one before the chain refuses. The cave is not a style flaw. It is your knee paying with cartilage what your thigh was supposed to pay with muscle, and unlike muscle, cartilage does not grow back stronger from the experience. There is a tempo signature in clean pistols worth copying from the athletes who own them: three seconds down, a still second at the bottom, two seconds up, no exceptions. The pause is not decoration; it deletes the stretch reflex that bounces mediocre reps out of the hole, and it forces the knee to own the angle statically before dynamically. Most failed pistols are failed pauses. Train the pause as its own rep and the full movement assembles itself around it within weeks.

The counterweight pistol is the honest halfway house of this family, and it deserves a defense. Hold a light weight, even a full water bottle, at arm's length, and the mass in front lets you sit into depth your ankle has not yet earned, while your knee trains the full range today instead of next season. The rule is accounting: the weight is a loan with a repayment schedule. Drop a little of it every two weeks as the ankle work pays out, and test monthly with empty hands. Loans are not cheating. Untracked loans are. Track yours and the pistol arrives with the ankle as a co-signer instead of a blocker.

Your advantage is the ratio, as always in this season: one leg, one body, and yours is the lightest body in the gym. Lean athletes collect pistols while men who squat double cannot do one, because their legs are strong in a currency this test does not accept. But the exchange only honors clean reps. A skinny guy bouncing on a lifted heel is spending the same counterfeit as everyone else. Your build gives you the cheapest honest pistol available. Buy it honestly and it is yours for life. One more dividend of your ratio: joint longevity in training. Deep knee work at bodyweight loads the joint in proportion to you, and a lighter you means the same skill practice at a friendlier absolute load, more often, for more years. The pistol is a skill some athletes age out of as they get heavier and stronger in other currencies. Your build can keep it on the menu for decades, and a skill you keep for decades becomes part of how you move through the world.
Sink with me, clean only. Forty seconds of deep split squats, heel down, knee tracking straight, pause at the bottom. This is the pistol, paid in installments. Go.

The five mistakes destroying your ankle and knee leverage. One: lifting the heel, bypassing the ankle and perching the whole load on your toes. Two: the knee caving inward, paying with cartilage what muscle owed. Three: bouncing out of the bottom, skipping the exact angle where pistol strength is manufactured. Four: the free foot touching down mid-rep, a silent second leg doing uncounted work. Five: refusing assistance, never using a box or a doorway for balance, so every session is falling practice instead of depth training. Use the box, pause the bottom, keep the heel planted. Assistance is not cheating; falling is not training. Mistake two, the cave, has a fix worth its own sentence: think of screwing your foot into the floor, big toe down, knee tracking over the middle toes, and if it still dives, your thigh is not yet strong enough for that depth, full stop. Raise the box, keep the tracking perfect, and let strength arrive at an angle your knee can supervise. Depth will come. Cartilage does not send thank-you notes for being skipped in the queue.

beats.text: ZERO CLEAN: A MISTAKE SPENDS YOU

scenes.narration: So, your clean count. Zero: a mistake is spending your depth, and its name is on the list. One to three clean: the chain holds end to end, now add volume. Over three clean on the weaker leg: your ankle and knee leverage is certified, and pistol country has your name on the deed. Retest in thirty days, weaker leg, full depth, first mistake ends the count. Put your clean reps in the comments. Just the number. Depth grades honesty at the bottom. Judge the month by receipts: box height lowered, pause held longer, wobble reduced, count grown. Any two of those is a month the chain genuinely improved, and most honest trainees collect three. The pistol's final gift is that it cannot be argued with at the bottom. Either you paused there, owned it, and stood, or the rep belongs to the honorable category of almost. Almost, compounded monthly, has a way of becoming always.
Heel down, knee honest, bottom paused. Clean pistols are built, not attempted. Subscribe, and bring me your new clean count in thirty days. This is {channel}. Train the cable.

title: 5 pistol squat Mistakes That Are Destroying Your ankle and knee leverage
